title: Model decay detection & procurement retainer playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable playbook that detects capability decay in external models (latency/quality/economic signals), triages signal sources, and triggers procurement retainer / fallback provisioning actions. This bridges model landscape monitoring with concrete procurement and Dedicated capacity triggers so product teams can avoid outages or quality regressions when third-party models degrade or become unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Detection rules implemented in monitoring: accuracy drift, 95th latency delta, token-cost spike, and availability loss
Playbook runbook drafted and reviewed by Eng/Legal/Finance/Procurement
Automation prototype that opens procurement retainer request and suggests fallback model variant in Console
Staging end-to-end test: simulated model decay triggers an alert and suggested actions appear in PM dashboard
RACI and SLAs documented for handoffs between Product, SRE, and Procurement
tasks: Define prioritized decay signals and thresholds (PM + Research)
Instrument Eval harness to run daily reference prompt set against model inventory
Implement alerting rules in Grafana/Alertmanager and map to PagerDuty runbook
Draft procurement retainer request template and acceptance criteria (Finance + Legal input)
Build Console UI mock for retainer suggestion and fallback model pinning
Create automation to open procurement ticket with suggested capacity level and duration
Run two-week shadow test on non-production traffic and record false-positive rate
Finalize playbook and run tabletop exercise with SRE/Account Execs/Support
stakeholders: Leah Kim (Eng - Serving Runtime) - alerts integration
metrics: MTTR for model-caused incidents (goal: <30m for detection->fallback decision)
False positive rate for decay alerts (goal: <10% after tuning)
Number of procurement retainers triggered per quarter
% of production requests routed to fallback model during incidents
Estimated cost delta per triggered retainer (billing realism check)
risks: High false positive sensitivity could cause unnecessary reserve spend
Legal timelines for rapid retainer activation may be longer than technical fallback
Vendor pricing or capacity may change between signal and activation window
Over-aggressive automation could open procurement tickets without human review
Edge cases in multi-tenant Dedicated pools where fallback capacity conflicts with other customers
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: finalize signal taxonomy and sample prompt set (PM+Research)
Week 3: implement detection rules in staging; wire alerts to internal channel
Week 4: shadow test automation that compiles suggested procurements (no live tickets)
Week 5: tabletop exercise with stakeholders; refine thresholds
Week 6: enable automated ticket creation to Procurement with approval gating
Week 7-8: pilot with 2 enterprise customers who opt into early-warning program
Post-pilot: iterate on thresholds, surface UI changes in Console, and roll to GA
